title: Electrolysis
examples: What is the difference between electrolysis in a liquid and in a water solution?
How do we predict what gas will form at the electrodes?
Does the state of the salt matter when we do electrolysis?

explain.say: Today we are learning about electrolysis in chemistry.
The electrodes are where the chemical changes happen.
At the cathode, reduction always happens, gaining electrons.
At the anode, oxidation always happens, losing electrons.
Molten salts conduct electricity through ions freely.
In an aqueous solution, water molecules can also react.

items: Water can be oxidized or reduced
It depends on the ions present

faq.q: Does the electricity always force the reaction to happen?
faq.a: Yes, electrolysis uses electrical energy to force non-spontaneous chemical reactions to occur. This is different from a simple chemical reaction.
asks: What is the purpose of electrolysis?

faq.q: If I use molten salt, are the ions more mobile than in water?
faq.a: In molten salts, the ions are free to move past each other without being surrounded by water molecules. This makes them very mobile.
asks: Is conductivity better in liquid or solid?
What is the difference in ion movement?

faq.q: Which reaction happens at the cathode, reduction or oxidation?
faq.a: Reduction always happens at the cathode. This means species gain electrons at this electrode.
asks: Do gains happen at the negative electrode?

faq.q: Can water react during electrolysis even if salts are present?
faq.a: Yes, water can react, especially if the ions present cannot be easily oxidized or reduced. The reaction with water is a possibility to consider.

faq.q: How do I predict what gas forms at the anode?
faq.a: You must compare the expected oxidation potentials of the ions present. The species that is more easily oxidized will react first.
asks: Which ion reacts first at the anode?

facts: Electrolysis uses electrical current to cause chemical decomposition.
Reduction (gain of electrons) occurs at the cathode.
Oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode.
Molten salts conduct electricity because ions are free to move.

quiz.say: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, what is produced at the cathode?
quiz.why: At the cathode, reduction occurs, and sodium ions have a very high tendency to gain electrons.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because hydrogen gas is usually formed when water is present, not from molten salts.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because chlorine gas is formed at the anode, not the cathode.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because the ions are consumed by the reaction, not left behind.

quiz.say: If an aqueous solution of copper sulfate is electrolyzed, what is the most likely product at the anode?
quiz.why: Even though copper ions are present, oxygen from the water is usually more easily oxidized than the copper ions.

wrong.1: This is incorrect because copper metal is a product at the cathode, not the anode.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because the sulfur component is usually stable under these conditions.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because the ions are in solution and will react, not remain as solid material.

quiz.say: When comparing molten vs aqueous electrolysis, what is a key difference in ion movement?

options.show: In molten salts, ions are completely free to move.
options.say: In molten salts, ions are completely free to move.

options.show: In aqueous solutions, ions are completely free.
options.say: In aqueous solutions, ions are completely free.

options.show: Both types of electrolysis have the same ion mobility.
options.say: Both types of electrolysis have the same ion mobility.

options.show: Only molten salts allow for redox reactions.
options.say: Only molten salts allow for redox reactions.

quiz.why: In molten salts, the absence of water molecules allows ions to move independently, unlike in water.

wrong.1: This is wrong because water molecules surround and stabilize the ions in solution.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the presence of water changes the electrical properties significantly.
wrong.3: This is wrong because aqueous solutions are very common for electrolysis.
